SMTO-CTX-0023 — Your task request is too long for the AI model to work with

GUID: 0480c0c6-70ec-4824-a1a5-bdd5aeb5a68e
Slug: goal-echo-exceeds-context
Domain: CTX · Subsystem: ctx

What happened

  • SMTO repeats your original request to the AI model on every step so it stays on track. Your request plus the task's other information no longer fit in the model's space. Your words were kept exactly; nothing was cut.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Open the stopped task and note which parts of the work it already finished. You only need to ask again for the parts that are still missing.
  2. Start a new task with a shorter request. Split a large job into smaller tasks, and attach long text as a file instead of pasting it into the message. A shorter request leaves the model enough space to also hold the task's progress.
  3. If the request can't be made shorter, ask the person who manages SMTO to route your work to a model with more space in Settings › Setup › Model routing. A model that can hold more text can keep your full request alongside the task's progress.

What success looks like

  • The new task runs its steps without this message.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them, with the size of your request, to the person who manages SMTO. Don't resubmit the same long request unchanged; it will stop at the same point.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • Context preparation could not fit the exact saved user goal, together with the required request state and reserved output, inside the model's context window; the goal is never truncated (legacy diagnostic, current capacity checks run in context preparation).

What this means

  • Appending the exact saved goal reminder makes the complete projected input plus reserved output exceed the model window; the original transcript and goal are not truncated. Context admission, storage and reading are separate from executing a tool mutation. Preserve existing task state and receipts; a context diagnostic does not authorize replay of earlier operations.

Why this can happen

  • Appending the exact saved goal reminder makes the complete projected input plus reserved output exceed the model window; the original transcript and goal are not truncated.

How to diagnose it

  • Compare goal-echo mode and its measured/estimated added tokens with the complete request budget; the reminder is distinct from stored transcript content.

How to fix it

  • Start a new task with a narrower goal, or route it to a model with a larger served context window (Settings > Setup > Model routing; lowering Output allowance also frees input space). The existing run keeps its captured goal and model profile, so resubmitting it unchanged will fail the same way; do not truncate the goal or bypass scope checks.
  • Start a new task with a deliberately narrower goal or a compatible larger-context model. The existing task preserves the original goal; do not truncate it silently or retry unchanged captured input.

Retry and execution caution

  • Correct the recorded cause, then inspect current state and existing receipts before requesting another attempt.

How to verify the fix

  • The full intended request and any enabled goal reminder fit before inference begins.

What not to do

  • Do not bypass scope or ownership checks to force a larger operation through.

Technical notes

  • Context admission, storage and reading are separate from executing a tool mutation. Preserve existing task state and receipts; a context diagnostic does not authorize replay of earlier operations.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
